title: Come, Shout Aloud the Father's Grace
description: Come, Shout Aloud the Father's Grace in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Ottiwell Heginbotham wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 644 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Rejoicing in God, our Father”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Come, shout a-loud the Fa-ther's grace, And sing the Sav-iour's love; Soon shall you join the glo-rious theme, In lofti-er strains a-bove.

lines: Come, shout aloud the Father's grace,
Soon shall you join the glorious theme,
Calls us his treasure and his joy,
My Father, God! and may these lips
Not thus could heaven's sweet harmony
Thanks to my God for every gift
And thanks eternal for that love

licence: Public domain: Ottiwell Heginbotham died in 1768.
credits: Words by Ottiwell Heginbotham (1744–1768), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
